JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a fundamentally sound, diversified healthcare franchise with strong competitive positions in oncology (Darzalex, Carvykti) and immunology (Tremfya), a 64-year dividend increase streak, and a recently raised 2026 guidance targeting ~$101B in revenue. However, the stock has re-rated significantly over the past year (P/E from ~18x to ~29x, P/B from ~5x to ~7.5x), placing it at the top of its own historical valuation range. While Q2 2026 results beat expectations and the pipeline is active, the current valuation already prices in much of the good news. Key risks include Stelara biosimilar erosion (760bp headwind), talc litigation overhang, Abiomed softness, and rising interest rates (10Y at 4.57%). The near-term catalyst of the Q2 beat and guidance raise has already been absorbed (stock at $250, up from $239 pre-earnings). Net income on a GAAP basis was flat YoY in Q2, and H1 2026 net earnings of $10.8B are down sharply from $16.5B a year ago, partly due to one-time items but still notable. The score reflects a quality franchise that is fairly-to-slightly-richly valued, with limited upside re-rating potential at current levels.

Johnson & Johnson experienced a mid-July stock pullback of approximately 2% following earnings results, but analysts view this as a buying opportunity. The company reported strong Q2 results with $25.31B in revenue (up 6.8% YOY), beat EPS expectations at $2.90, and raised full-year guidance.

Johnson & Johnson reported Q2 sales of $25.31 billion, up 6.6% from a year earlier and above analysts' average estimate of about $25.05 billion. Adjusted earnings were $2.90 per share, up 4.7% from a year ago and topping analyst expectations of $2.85
Net earnings for the first six months of 2026 were $10.8B compared with $16.5B a year earlier
TREMFYA delivered strong growth through market share gains and inflammatory bowel disease launch momentum. Sales surging 73% to $2 billion
Abiomed faced near-term pressure with a 2% decline, as physicians responded cautiously to a U.K. clinical study on heart recovery pump usage
STELARA biosimilar competition created a 460-basis-point drag on overall sales and a 760-basis-point impact on Innovative Medicine
The company now expects operational sales growth of 6.5% to 7.1% (midpoint of $100.6 billion), reported sales $100.8 billion to $101.4 billion
Johnson & Johnson has a 64 year record of annual dividend increases and currently pays US$1.34 per quarter
The affirmed US$45m talc verdict and broader product liability exposure, add uncertainty to future cash flows
Ken Griffin increased his stake in Johnson & Johnson by 146% in Q1 2026, bringing his total holdings to nearly 2 million shares
